author: product-requirements-expert
title: Specialty directory lists each specialty with the veterinarians holding it
summary: A read-only specialty directory page lists every stored specialty by name, each with the veterinarians who hold it shown by full name, all on one page with no pagination — the inverse of the veterinarian directory.
acceptance_criteria: Opening the specialty directory lists every specialty by its stored name, each with the veterinarians who hold it shown by full name (first name then last name, e.g. 'Helen Leary')
A veterinarian holding no specialty does not appear on the page: the directory lists specialties and the veterinarians grouped beneath them, not the full veterinarian roster
All specialties render on a single page with no pagination
Specialties are presented in a stable order rather than an arbitrary one
A specialty is listed because it is stored, independently of how many veterinarians hold it
non_goals: Managing veterinarians or specialties through the application (NG-2 unchanged)
notes: Read-only view over the existing Vet/Specialty model — no schema or write path. This slice does not modify the shared navigation (REQ-SYS-001); the page is reached by its own route. file_targets are best-effort: whether the route lives on a new SpecialtyController or the existing VetController, and whether a SpecialtyRepository is added or specialties are grouped from the cached vet collection, is a design decision for system-design-expert.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Read-only view inside the existing `vet` feature package; no new module, pattern, or bounded context. Both open design questions resolve to established precedents. (1) New `SpecialtyController` (not an added route on `VetController`): the Naming rule prefixes a Web controller by the surface it serves, and the specialty directory is a distinct surface answering the inverse question; folding it into VetController would give one controller two unrelated surfaces (system-design Contracts already notes VetController serves the paged HTML + the serialized route). (2) A `SpecialtyRepository` IS required and grouping from the cached vet collection alone is insufficient — acceptance edge case 2 ('a specialty is listed because it is stored, independently of how many veterinarians hold it') demands the page be driven by the stored specialty set, but specialties are reachable only through Vet's unidirectional @ManyToMany (Vet.java:47-50), so an unheld specialty can never surface from the vet graph. SpecialtyRepository mirrors PetTypeRepository (Spring Data JpaRepository returning the lookup rows ORDER BY name — PetTypeRepository.java:36-37), which also satisfies the stable-order edge case. The vets-per-specialty inversion is presentation view-model assembly in the controller (analogous to VetController.addPaginationModel), not a domain rule, so the no-business-rule-in-controller checklist item is not tripped.
integration_points: New GET route for the specialty directory (own path, e.g. /specialties.html); this slice does not touch shared navigation REQ-SYS-001 per the prd-entry
SpecialtyRepository.findAll ordered by name is the authoritative specialty list (drives which rows appear)

Reuses VetRepository.findAll() — the non-paged @Cacheable("vets") variant (VetRepository.java:44-46) — to source vets; the controller inverts vet->specialties into specialty->vets, dropping vets whose specialty set does not contain the row (which naturally omits vets holding none)
Full-name rendering uses the same form the vet template already uses: vet.firstName + ' ' + vet.lastName (vetList.html)
Vets within each specialty rendered in a stable order (order by last/first name)

patterns.description: Repository per lookup entity returning rows ORDER BY name — precedent for SpecialtyRepository (grounded by Read; IDE oracle not connected on this run)

Web controller adapting one HTTP surface with private view-model assembly helpers — precedent for SpecialtyController and for keeping the grouping as presentation assembly (grounded by Read; oracle not connected)

risks.risk: Grouping the page from the cached vet collection alone would pass against the current seed (all three seeded specialties happen to be held) but silently violate edge case 2 — an unheld specialty would vanish from the directory.
risks.mitigation: SpecialtyRepository.findAll(ORDER BY name) is the authoritative row source; the cached vet collection supplies only the vets grouped beneath each row. A test seeding an unheld specialty pins this.

risks.risk: The vet-per-specialty inversion could be read as a business rule landing in a controller (checklist: no business rule in a web controller).
risks.mitigation: It is presentation view-model assembly, not a domain invariant or validation — keep it in a private helper mirroring VetController.addPaginationModel; introduce no Specialty->Vet domain reference.

notes: Caching, stated explicitly as requested: the existing vet cache (@Cacheable("vets") on VetRepository, declared by CacheConfiguration) DOES apply to the vet half of this page when the controller sources vets via VetRepository.findAll(), but does NOT and cannot cover the specialty enumeration — the authoritative row set comes from the new SpecialtyRepository, which is uncached. No new cache region is added: caching specialties is not required for this read-only slice and would replicate the eviction-less pattern already flagged as an open question (system-design Open Question 5); leave it out under consistency-over-novelty and demand-driven scope. No ADR: no hard-to-reverse trade-off — both design questions land on existing patterns. No ubiquitous-language change: Specialty and Veterinarian are already canonical. system-design.md left unchanged at triage (it is current-state/derived-from-code); doc-sync should add Contracts rows for SpecialtyController and SpecialtyRepository and wire REQ-SPEC-001 into the Implements column (also onto Vet and Specialty) once the code lands. IDE semantic oracle not in this dispatch's tool set — resolution claims grounded by Read of the cited files, the weaker basis.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: Stable order (prd.md Edge case 1) has no assertion. The mock for findSpecialties() happens to return [dentistry, radiology, surgery] in alphabetical order, but no test asserts the rendered order of specialties in the HTML response. An ORDER BY regression in SpecialtyRepository would pass all four tests undetected because containsString assertions are order-agnostic. A test must assert the relative position of specialty names in the response body, or seed the mock in non-alphabetical order and verify sorting was applied.

Vet-to-specialty grouping is not asserted. theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldShowVeterinariansByFullName checks that 'Helen Leary' and 'Linda Douglas' appear anywhere on the page, but not that Helen Leary appears under radiology and Linda Douglas under dentistry. If the controller grouped both vets under the wrong specialty, all four tests would still pass. An assertion on content ordering (radiology header before 'Helen Leary', dentistry header before 'Linda Douglas') would close the gap without complex DOM parsing.

The within-specialty vet sort (Comparator by last/first name in SpecialtyController line 69) is never exercised. Each specialty in the test fixture holds at most one vet, so the Comparator is never invoked. Adding a second vet under one specialty and asserting their rendered order would cover this code path and pin the sort contract.

author: code-quality-reviewer

findings.description: holds() compares specialties by name rather than by canonical ID. The vets arrive via the @Cacheable("vets") variant of VetRepository, so their Specialty instances are JPA objects from a previous session — not the same references as the Specialty objects returned by specialtyRepository.findSpecialties(). Name equality works only because specialty names happen to be unique; there is no unique constraint enforcing that invariant, and the comparison surprises anyone who knows that entity identity is the ID. A reader who sees held.getName().equals(specialty.getName()) must reason about why an entity field, not the entity's identity, is the matching key.
findings.fix: Replace held.getName().equals(specialty.getName()) with held.getId().equals(specialty.getId()). This makes the intent (same stored specialty row) explicit and works correctly whether or not the vet collection is served from the second-level cache.

author: code-quality-reviewer

findings.description: assertRenderedInOrder() calls body.indexOf(fragment) starting from index 0 on every iteration, using `previous` only for the comparison — not as the search start. The Javadoc says 'each strictly after the previous one', but the implementation finds each fragment's first occurrence in the entire string. If a fragment appeared at two positions in the body (one before and one after the preceding fragment), indexOf would return the earlier position and the assertion would fail even though the order is actually correct. The method happens to be correct for all current fixtures because each fragment appears exactly once, but it does not match its documented contract.
findings.fix: Change `int index = body.indexOf(fragment);` to `int index = body.indexOf(fragment, previous + 1);`. When `previous` is -1 (initial value), `previous + 1` is 0, so the first search still starts at the beginning.
